Cautiously positive: The FOMC cut the target range 25 bps to 4.25–4.50% while continuing balance‑sheet runoff, framing the move as data‑dependent with risks “roughly in balance.” This mix aligns with flexible inflation‑targeting and risk‑management practice (Svensson and Woodford, 2005) and is broadly consistent with Taylor‑rule logic (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler) given inflation still somewhat above 2% and a modest uptick in unemployment near the natural rate. Easing labor‑market tightness lowers real marginal cost in the New Keynesian Phillips Curve, supporting gradual disinflation, while implementation via IORB at 4.4% and ON RRP at 4.25% reflects modern floor‑system operations (Goodfriend, 2002). A single dissent to hold rates underscores time‑inconsistency/inflation‑bias risks and tempers the tone. Net takeaway: cautiously supportive of growth with vigilance on inflation.
